title: Stablecoin flows and spillovers to FX markets (BIS Working Papers No 1340)
date_evidence: BIS Working Papers No 1340 Stablecoin flows and spillovers to FX markets ... Monetary and Economic Department March 2026 ... March 25, 2026
key_claim: Using four USD-pegged stablecoins and 27 fiat currencies, more than 70% of cumulative net inflows into stablecoins originate from non-USD currencies; a 1% exogenous increase in net stablecoin inflows raises stablecoin-vs-spot dollar parity deviations by about 40 basis points, depreciates the local currency and widens covered-interest-parity dollar premia, with spillovers growing disproportionately when intermediaries suffer losses.
notes: Tier 1 primary; the quantified FX-spillover evidence anchoring the signal. Authors at BIS and IMF.

title: From money market funds to stablecoins: lessons for central banks (Bank of Korea International Conference, Seoul)
date_evidence: Isabel Schnabel ... delivered a speech titled 'From money market funds to stablecoins: lessons for central banks' at the ... Bank of Korea International Conference in Seoul on June 1, 2026.
key_claim: In jurisdictions with weaker monetary credibility, residents may increasingly hold dollar-denominated claims, intensifying currency substitution and endangering monetary sovereignty by weakening domestic monetary policy; broad dollar-stablecoin adoption could amplify the international transmission of US monetary policy and challenges the lender-of-last-resort function in a tokenised system that operates around the clock; global stablecoin market capitalisation is near $300 billion, with USDT and USDC about 90%.
notes: Tier 1; the most recent (1 June 2026) central-bank framing of stablecoins as a monetary-sovereignty threat. Page is long/JS-heavy; date from WebSearch snippet and dated URL slug sp260601.

title: As Emerging Markets Attract More Nonbank Capital, They Also Face New Challenges (GFSR April 2026, Chapter 2)
date_evidence: IMF Blog ... based on Chapter 2 of the April 2026 Global Financial Stability Report on Capital Flows to Emerging Markets ... 2026/04/07
key_claim: Emerging-market funding is increasingly sourced from nonbank and parallel channels, delivering benefits but raising vulnerability to sudden capital-flow reversals; portfolio flows to EMs have risen roughly eightfold since the global financial crisis, with about 80% provided by nonbanks.
notes: Tier 1; corroborates the EM capital-flow-reversal vulnerability that stablecoin channels can amplify. Cited for the capital-flow context, not as a stablecoin-specific claim.

title: Monetary Sovereignty Faces New Challenges From Stablecoins
date_evidence: URL .../our-expertise/insights/2026/feb/monetary-sovereignty-stablecoins.html ; WebSearch result: 'The Oliver Wyman Monetary Sovereignty report on stablecoins was published in February 2026'
key_claim: Stablecoins threaten monetary sovereignty through three channels (reduced policy traction, pressure on bank deposits, amplified crisis-time capital flight) and may compress the historical dollarisation timeline from years to months; regulators face three strategic choices - Ban (China, Gulf states), Compete (CBDC or licensed domestic stablecoin, e.g. Japan) or Adapt (authorisation, e.g. the UK).
notes: Tier 2 consultancy. Single structural anchor (web article February 2026, ~3.5 months); supplies the policy-choice framing and the years-to-months compression. Underlying full report dated Nov 2025; web article is the Feb 2026 edition.

title: How stablecoins are extending the monetary power of the United States
key_claim: Stablecoin transaction volume grew from about $565 billion in 2020 to roughly $11 trillion in 2025; about 99% of stablecoins in circulation were dollar-denominated as of November 2025; flows reach roughly 7-8% of GDP in Latin America and the Caribbean and in Africa and the Middle East, where stablecoin holdings rose from near zero in 2020 to between 2% and 3% of total deposits by 2024 - a 'digital dollarisation' that also lowers short-term Treasury yields and extends US monetary power.
notes: Tier 2 institutional research blog (LSE; PhD-economist authors with original on-chain analysis); supplies EM penetration figures and the US-power-extension counter-framing.

title: Stablecoins Could Pose Major Risks to Monetary Policy, ECB Paper Warns
date_evidence: Stablecoins Could Pose Major Risks to Monetary Policy, ECB Paper Warns ... bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-03-03/
key_claim: An ECB working paper warns that significant dollar-stablecoin adoption could disrupt monetary-policy transmission and amplify cross-border spillovers of US monetary policy.
notes: Tier 3 journalism reporting the ECB working paper on stablecoins and monetary-policy transmission.

title: ECB warns stablecoins risk financial stability and dollar dominance
date_evidence: ECB warns Stablecoins risk financial stability and Dollar dominance | FXStreet ... url ...-202606021117 (2026-06-02)
key_claim: Coverage of the 1 June 2026 ECB intervention framing stablecoins as posing three risks: bank runs and fire sales, disruption of monetary-policy transmission, and the cementing of US dollar dominance.
notes: Tier 3 specialist financial press; corroborates the market salience of the June 2026 ECB warning.
